Source: He has a high-frequency bilateral hand tremor elicited on finger-to-nose testing.
On physical exam, his temperature is 98.6°F (37.0°C), blood pressure is 159/84, pulse is 74/min, and respirations are 12/min.
A 51-year-old man presents to his primary care provider for intermittent shaking of his hands.
The patient smokes half a pack per day of cigarettes and drinks 2-3 beers throughout the day.
For the last several years he has noticed this "shaking" when he brushes his teeth and prepares a cup of coffee in the morning.
The shaking then gradually improves over the course of the day.
His only home medication is pravastatin.
His neurological exam is otherwise unremarkable.
His family history is significant for Parkinson disease in his father.
His medical history is otherwise notable for hypertension and hyperlipidemia.
